cells.tense: You are standing at the door of something finished, and your hands have gone lighter.
cells.act: sit with what the heart already knows
cells.ask: Give some unhurried time this week to how that ending landed in you — no deciding, no fixing. Let it take as long as it takes.
cells.core:
Something has ended, and the whole of how it landed is available — not one feeling about it but the full range, and the connection to what is done holds steady while the grip eases. That is the release working: the hand opens because the thing is complete, not because you made yourself stop holding.

The quiet that follows is not blank. It carries your own weight, and it can rest without being turned into a lesson. The one move that keeps this honest is giving the sense of it real time — not the version you would say if asked, the one the body carries — until your words and your body say the same thing. Then whatever comes next comes from the clear place.
cells.sheetLine: What ended is finished, and your hands are open.
cells.verb: letting a finished thing be finished
cells.place: at the door you are standing in after the closing

cells.tense: You are bracing for a release you keep trying to finish before it has finished itself.
cells.act: hold the first resource in your hand before investing it
cells.ask: Before releasing one thing, hold it a while — long enough to see what it was for — then let it go once, cleanly.
cells.core:
The release has gotten ahead of what is complete. You are shutting doors that are still open and calling it peace, or rehearsing the goodbye while the thing still has its weight. The whole feeling got turned into a verb — being done with it — and the doing is lapping the actual ending. Nothing has been released; a door keeps getting closed and reopened, and the grip underneath is tighter for the motion.

Slow down to the size of your hands. Take one thing and hold it for what it actually is before you end it — an hour, a week, whatever it takes to see it plainly — then release that one. The rest can wait. If what a thing was for will not come clear, that is not a failure; it just is not finished, and it will tell you when it is.
cells.sheetLine: You keep closing a door that isn't shut.
cells.verb: letting a finished thing be finished
cells.place: at the door you are standing in after the closing

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that has already closed behind you, and your weight hasn't shifted yet.
cells.act: catch the first spark before you point it anywhere
cells.ask: When something in you leans forward this week, decide nothing about it. Let the leaning be enough.
cells.core:
The ending happened; the heart has not been told. You keep standing at the door waiting for a feeling that would let you leave, and nothing comes, because the thing to release already went. From inside it looks like nothing has changed — everything looks the same through a window as through an open door, and you are looking through the window.

Presence starts smaller than feeling. No asking your body to feel the release before it does — just letting the first flicker of a lean, toward anything or anyone or a fresh minute, do its thing with no plan attached. One unpointed spark. It does not have to become anything. Letting something start while it is still nothing is how a door gets remembered as behind you.
cells.sheetLine: The ending happened, and the heart hasn't been told yet.
cells.verb: letting a finished thing be finished

cells.tense: You are laying something down cleanly, and the phrase you use for it is that it was time.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: When the pull comes to let something go quietly, notice — privately, no announcement — and follow that. Or don't.
cells.core:
There is a way you end things that keeps the books fair. You count what you owe, you return it before anyone asks, you let go cleanly so nobody carries more than their share — and asked why, you would say things resolved themselves, or it was time. The compass that keeps this steady is yours. You just do not sign for it.

The act is a pause before the next quiet release: notice your own hand in the balancing, and hold that fact to yourself before you move. That is the whole difference — not a scene, not a speech. A witness inside, counting along with you. Then act, or do not. The awareness stays either way.
cells.sheetLine: You let it go cleanly. You put it down to timing.
